description:
Worth defending: src/notification.rs:146-152 declares CalendarAlert.recurrence_id without #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]. So when recurrence_id is None, it serializes as 'recurrenceId': null on the wire, not omitted.

This is intentional and load-bearing: per draft-ietf-jmap-calendars-26 §6.4, the receiver uses the presence-or-absence of the recurrenceId field to distinguish recurring from non-recurring events. If we omitted the field on null, a non-recurring CalendarAlert would be indistinguishable from a serialization that simply forgot to include the field.

A 'clippy clean-up' or 'consistency PR' could trivially flag this as inconsistent with neighboring fields and 'fix' it by adding skip_serializing_if. That would silently break receivers.

The verifying test is calendar_alert_recurrence_id_null_for_non_recurring (tests/types_test.rs:1296-1319). Keep both the field-attribute decision and the test in sync.

Cross-reference: workspace 'always serialize null vs skip' pattern. This is the precedent the same crate's PrincipalCalendarsCapability.account_id uses (capability.rs:121, also documented as 'required-and-nullable').
title: decision: CalendarAlert.recurrence_id deliberately serializes as null (no skip_serializing_if)
